label: prf:fiber-adjoint-involution
title: Proof of Fiber--adjoint-fiber involution
html:
The Frobenius isomorphism A \cong A^{\vee} sends a \mapsto \int_A \circ \mu(a \otimes -), which is non-degenerate by the Frobenius--Hopf axiom.

By (rank-1 projectors as a coadjoint orbit), the traceless components of rank-1 projectors give an involution 2\sigma(\rho) in \mathrm{End}(V) and identify \mathbb{P}(V) \cong G/T with a closed coadjoint orbit in \mathrm{Ad}(A).

(3) Observability. Suppose there exists a non-zero morphism f \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A). Such a morphism would represent a G-invariant element in the adjoint representation. By the \mathrm{SU}(2) emergence theorem (\mathrm{SU}(2) emergence), the reconstructed gauge group is G \cong \mathrm{SU}(2), and \mathrm{Ad}(A) carries the irreducible adjoint representation \mathfrak{su}(2) (dimension 3). By Schur's lemma, the only intertwining morphism from the trivial representation \mathbf{1} to an irreducible non-trivial representation is the zero morphism. Therefore f = 0, contradicting our assumption.

Hence \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0. The non-degeneracy of \int_A excludes any hidden global symmetry: there is no non-trivial invariant section of the adjoint bundle. \square
